# Pix

An image viewer: one picture, as large as the window allows, and the rest of its folder a key press away.

## Install (Windows)

Open **PowerShell** (a normal window - administrator rights are not needed) and run:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.ps1 | iex
```

That is the whole install. A window opens where you can change the folder and choose shortcuts,
PATH and file types, then press **Install**. It downloads Pix 0.1.2, checks every file
against the SHA-256 in the [install manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/manifest.json), and installs for your user only.

What it does:

- creates the install folder and places the binaries there
- unblocks them and makes sure they are executable
- creates desktop / Start menu shortcuts
- adds the install folder to your user PATH
- registers itself to open `.png`, `.apng`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.jfif`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.bmp`, `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.svg`, `.ico`, `.tga`, `.qoi`, `.pnm`, `.pbm`, `.pgm`, `.ppm`, `.dds`, `.exr`, `.hdr`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.wmv`, `.flv`, `.mpg`, `.mpeg`, `.ts`, `.m2ts`, `.mts`, `.3gp`, `.ogv` files (under Open with; the default only where no other program has claimed the type)
- writes an install manifest listing everything it installed and where
- adds an uninstaller and an updater next to the binaries, and an entry in Settings > Apps

### Options

The window covers the folder and the `NO_*` choices. For a scripted install, or one without the
window, set these in the same PowerShell window *before* the install command:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `$env:INSTALL_VERSION = '1.2.3'` | install a specific version from the [history](#versions) |
| `$env:INSTALL_DIR = 'D:\Apps\Pix'` | install somewhere other than `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix` |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_SHORTCUTS = '1'` | skip the desktop / Start menu shortcuts |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_PATH = '1'` | do not add anything to your user PATH |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_ASSOCIATIONS = '1'` | do not register Pix to open any file types |
| `$env:INSTALL_FORCE = '1'` | reinstall even if this version is already installed |
| `$env:INSTALL_SKIP_CHECKS = '1'` | install even if this computer does not meet the system requirements |
| `$env:INSTALL_QUIET = '1'` | no window: ask nothing and report in PowerShell only |
| `$env:INSTALL_CLOSE_APPS = '1'` | close Pix if it is running and holds a file the update replaces |

Updates and reinstalls remember the `INSTALL_NO_*` choices of the last install. To get shortcuts,
the PATH entry or file types back, set that variable to `'0'` and run the install command again.

### What gets installed

| File | Kind | Version | Size | Installed to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pix.exe` | native executable | 0.1.2 | 62.7 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix\pix.exe` |
| `pix-ffmpeg-windows-x86_64.zip` | archive (unpacked) | 0.1.2 | 52.1 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix\ffmpeg\` |
| `pix-ffmpeg-record-windows-x86_64.zip` | archive (unpacked) | 0.1.2 | 5.5 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix\ffmpeg-record\` |
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` | file | 0.1.2 | 0.1 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix\THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` |

Everything installed is recorded in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pix\install-manifest.json`, and a copy
in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs\pix.json`.

### Other programs finding Pix

Installs are independent, so Pix can sit next to other programs from the same
installer. To start it from one of them without depending on PATH, read
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs\pix.json` and use `commands.<name>.path` - an absolute path to the
executable (the `.cmd` launcher for a jar). Missing file means not installed. Pass arguments
as usual; from Java use `new ProcessBuilder(path, args...)`, and for a `.cmd` launcher run it
as `cmd.exe /c path args...`.

### Update

Open **sibarum apps** from the Start menu. It lists everything installed this way, with **Update**,
**Change...** (folder, shortcuts, PATH, file types), **Remove** and **Update all**. Or update from PowerShell:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Pix\update.cmd"
```

Checks GitHub for newer versions of the binaries and installs them after asking. Use
`-Check` to only look, `-Yes` to skip the question.

An update that fails or is interrupted puts back the version you had, exactly as it was. If the computer
went off halfway, the next install or update first finishes putting it back.

### Reporting a problem

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Pix\diagnose.cmd"
```

Writes a report about this computer and prints where it is: Windows version, processor, memory, the displays
(resolution, refresh rate, scaling, HDR), each GPU as DXGI / Direct3D 12 and as Vulkan see it, whether a
flip-model swapchain can be created, the Vulkan present modes, implicit Vulkan layers, and what is installed.
Nothing is sent anywhere; your user name is replaced by `%USERPROFILE%`. Read it, then attach it to [your bug report](https://github.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/issues/new).
`-Copy` also puts it on the clipboard. Without installing, run `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/diagnose.ps1 | iex`. A failed
install writes the same report by itself.

### Uninstall

Use **Settings > Apps > Pix > Uninstall**, or:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Pix\uninstall.cmd"
```

The uninstaller reads the install manifests in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs`, so it removes exactly
what was installed - files, shortcuts, PATH entries, file types and the Apps entry. Files you added to
the install folder are left alone. `uninstall.cmd -List` shows every install it knows about
and `-All` removes them all.

### Is it safe to run a script from the internet?

Read it first - it is one file: [`install.ps1`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.ps1). Downloads are only
accepted when their SHA-256 matches the manifest, and the manifest and script live in this
repository.

## Install (Linux)

Open a terminal and run (no `sudo`: it installs for your user only):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.sh | sh
```

It downloads Pix 0.1.2, checks every file against the SHA-256 in the
[install manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/manifest.json), and installs into `~/.local/opt/pix`. It needs `curl` (or
`wget`), `tar` and `sha256sum`, which every desktop distribution has.

What it does:

- creates the install folder and places the binaries there, executable
- adds Pix to your applications menu
- puts a launcher on your desktop, if you have a Desktop folder
- links `pix` into `~/.local/bin`, so it runs from a terminal (a link is never put over a file that is not its own)
- registers itself to open `.png`, `.apng`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.jfif`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.bmp`, `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.svg`, `.ico`, `.tga`, `.qoi`, `.pnm`, `.pbm`, `.pgm`, `.ppm`, `.dds`, `.exr`, `.hdr`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.wmv`, `.flv`, `.mpg`, `.mpeg`, `.ts`, `.m2ts`, `.mts`, `.3gp`, `.ogv` files (under Open With; the default only where no other program is)
- writes an install manifest listing everything it installed and where
- adds `uninstall.sh` and `update.sh` next to the binaries

### System requirements

- a x86_64 processor (`uname -m` says `x86_64`)

The installer checks these before it downloads anything large and stops if one is not met. To install anyway, run it as `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.sh | INSTALL_SKIP_CHECKS=1 sh`.

### Options

Set these for the `sh` that runs the script, as in `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.sh | INSTALL_NO_PATH=1 sh`:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `INSTALL_VERSION=1.2.3` | install a specific version from the [history](#versions) |
| `INSTALL_DIR=/opt/pix` | install somewhere other than `~/.local/opt/pix` |
| `INSTALL_NO_SHORTCUTS=1` | no menu entry or desktop launcher |
| `INSTALL_NO_PATH=1` | link nothing into `~/.local/bin` |
| `INSTALL_NO_ASSOCIATIONS=1` | do not register Pix to open any file types |
| `INSTALL_FORCE=1` | reinstall even if this version is already installed |
| `INSTALL_SKIP_CHECKS=1` | install even if this computer does not meet the system requirements |

Updates and reinstalls remember the `INSTALL_NO_*` choices of the last install. To get them back,
set that variable to `0` and run the install command again.

### What gets installed

| File | Kind | Version | Size | Installed to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pix` | native executable | 0.1.2 | 64.2 MB | `~/.local/opt/pix/pix` |
| `pix-ffmpeg-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | archive (unpacked) | 0.1.2 | 56.5 MB | `~/.local/opt/pix/ffmpeg/` |
| `pix-ffmpeg-record-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | archive (unpacked) | 0.1.2 | 4.3 MB | `~/.local/opt/pix/ffmpeg-record/` |
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` | file | 0.1.2 | 0.1 MB | `~/.local/opt/pix/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` |

Everything installed is recorded in `~/.local/opt/pix/install-manifest.json`, and a copy in
`~/.local/share/vexelray-installer/installs/pix.json`, the same record the Windows installer writes: other programs
find Pix through `commands.<name>.path` in it.

### Update

```sh
"$HOME/.local/opt/pix/update.sh"
```

Checks for a newer version and installs it after asking. `--check` only looks, `--yes` does not ask.
An update that fails or is interrupted puts back the version you had, exactly as it was; if the
computer went off halfway, the next install or update first finishes putting it back.

### Uninstall

```sh
"$HOME/.local/opt/pix/uninstall.sh"
```

Removes exactly what was installed: files, the menu entry and desktop launcher, the links in
`~/.local/bin` and the file types. Files you added to the install folder are left alone. `--list`
shows every install it knows about, `--all` removes them all, `--yes` does not ask. Report problems at https://github.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/issues/new.

### Is it safe to pipe a script into sh?

Read it first - it is one file: [`install.sh`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/pix/install.sh). Downloads are only accepted when
their SHA-256 matches the manifest, and the manifest and the script live in this repository. It never
asks for root, and writes nowhere outside your home folder unless `INSTALL_DIR` says so.

A macOS installer is planned; the manifest is already organised per platform.

Current version: **0.1.2**. The full history of published versions, with the files,
